q-82020.name: Question 1
q-82020.problem: Rewrite the statement $¬((¬P∧¬Q)∨(P∧¬Q))$ using De Morgan's laws.
q-82020.worked_solution:
De Morgan's laws state that

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)≡¬P∨¬Q, \\ ¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∧¬Q.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((¬P∧¬Q)∨(P∧¬Q)) & ≡¬(¬P∧¬Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q) \\  & ≡(¬(¬P)∨¬(¬Q))∧(¬P∨¬(¬Q)) \\  & ≡(P∨Q)∧(¬P∨Q)\end{aligned}
$$

q-82020.html:
Question 1
?

Rewrite the statement ¬((¬P∧¬Q)∨(P∧¬Q)) using De Morgan's laws.

a
(P∨Q)∧(¬P∨Q)
b
(P∧Q)∧(¬P∧Q)
c
(P∨Q)∨(¬P∨Q)
d
(P∧Q)∨(¬P∨Q)
e
(¬P∨Q)∧(P∨¬Q)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's laws state that

¬(P∧Q)≡¬P∨¬Q,¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∧¬Q.

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

¬((¬P∧¬Q)∨(P∧¬Q))≡¬(¬P∧¬Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q)≡(¬(¬P)∨¬(¬Q))∧(¬P∨¬(¬Q))≡(P∨Q)∧(¬P∨Q)

q-129542.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(Q∧P)≡¬P∨¬Q, \\ ¬(Q∨P)≡¬P∧¬Q.\end{aligned}

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∨(B∧C)) & ≡¬A∧¬(B∧C) \\  & ≡¬A∧(¬B∨¬C)\end{aligned}
$$

q-171017.name: Question 3
q-171017.problem:
$\,$ $7=5$ or $-3\ge 0.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
q-171017.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(7=5\text{ or }-3\ge 0) & ≡¬((7=5)∨(-3\ge 0)) \\  & ≡¬(7=5)∧¬(-3\ge 0) \\  & ≡(7\ne 5)∧(-3<0) \\  & ≡7\ne 5\text{ and }-3<0.\end{aligned}

q-171017.html:
Question 3
?

7=5 or −3≥0.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
7≠5 or −3>0
b
7≠5 and −3>0
c
7≠5 and −3<0
d
7=5 and −3<0
e
7≠5 or −3≤0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(7=5 or −3≥0)≡¬((7=5)∨(−3≥0))≡¬(7=5)∧¬(−3≥0)≡(7≠5)∧(−3<0)≡7≠5 and −3<0.

q-182617.name: Question 4
q-182617.problem:
$\,$ $5$ is integer or $5$ is positive.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
q-182617.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(5\text{ is integer}\text{ or }5\text{ is positive}) & ≡¬((5\text{ is integer})∨(5\text{ is positive})) \\  & ≡¬(5\text{ is integer})∧¬(5\text{ is positive}) \\  & ≡(5\text{ is not integer})∧(5\text{ is not positive}) \\  & ≡5\text{ is not integer}\text{ and }5\text{ is not positive}.\end{aligned}
$$

?

5 is integer or 5 is positive.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a

b
5 is not integer and 5 is not positive
c
5 is integer and 5 is positive
d
5 is not integer or 5 is not positive
e
5 is not integer or 5 is positive
Submit
Incorrect

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B

q-182627.html:
Question 5
?

n is not prime or n⧸|24.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
n is prime or n|24
b
n is not prime and n⧸|24
c
n is prime and n|24
d
n is not prime or n|24
e
n is prime or n⧸|24
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(n is not prime or n⧸|24)≡¬((n is not prime)∨(n⧸|24))≡¬(n is not prime)∧¬(n⧸|24)≡(n is prime)∧(n|24)≡n is prime and n|24.
